rationale: Anytype documents a localhost API bundled with the desktop app and a CLI that runs Anytype as a headless server for automation. It also has an official MCP server for AI assistants and an agents skill that lets assistants "read, search, and modify Objects", backed by a published, versioned OpenAPI spec. That covers both read and write without touching the GUI. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agent read/write works headlessly in practice.

A live probe confirms an llms.txt at doc.anytype.io/llms.txt (HTTP 200) that indexes the docs as raw .md pages, which an agent can follow directly. Agent-oriented material backs it up: an agents skill documented for dropping into Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools, an AGENTS.md in the repo, and a machine-readable OpenAPI v2 spec described as 'built for agents and humans.' missing for 10: no evidence of an llms-full.txt or an llms.txt on the developers.anytype.io API portal, and no independent community corroboration of agents actually using these docs.

The evidence shows no built-in AI that generates insights or suggestions from a user's data inside Anytype. The AI-related items (MCP server, agents skill, local API) let external assistants such as Claude Code or Cursor read and modify Anytype data from outside the app, which is not in-product AI. Queries and Graph are deterministic, non-AI features, so they do not count either.

There is no evidence of a native automation feature in Anytype, such as triggers, schedules, or rules that run on their own in the background. The headless CLI 'for automation and scripting' and the local API are developer building blocks. The agents skill relies on external agent tools like Claude Code, a user-side workaround. Self-updating Queries and background sync are adjacent features, not user-defined automations.

The evidence shows only external-agent integrations: an MCP server, an agents skill toolkit for Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools, and a local API that outside AI assistants can call. None of these is a built-in AI assistant inside Anytype that users can delegate tasks to. The chat features are user-to-user messaging, and the GitHub "Agents" mention refers to extensibility, not an in-app assistant.

The developer portal explicitly states that the first-party Anytype CLI can 'run Anytype as a headless server for automation and scripting,' which covers the core of the story. A local API, an MCP server and an agents skill that scripts against Anytype data back up the automation surface. missing for 10: detailed CLI/headless setup documentation, explicit CI pipeline guidance or examples (e.g., auth/key provisioning in CI), independent or hands-on corroboration of headless operation.

The evidence shows Anytype exposing its own data to external AI assistants through an official MCP server, a local API, and an agents skill. That is the server role. Nothing documents Anytype itself connecting to third-party MCP servers or using their tools. A knowledge-base app could plausibly ship an AI assistant with MCP client support, so the axis applies, and the server-side evidence does not transfer to this story.

Anytype's official developer portal documents an MCP server that lets AI assistants interact with Anytype's API through natural language, backed by the local API bundled with the desktop app. Since Anytype is a knowledge app rather than an agent, the MCP-server axis applies. The evidence is only a one-line description, filed under an 'examples/featured' path. missing for 10: details on setup and client configuration, the exposed tool list and its read/write scope, and independent or hands-on corroboration that agents connect successfully.
